title: Soft the Weaver (Português)
summary: In a quiet village lived a gentle, simple-minded weaver named Mantharaka, known to all as Soft because of his mild and compliant nature. ... [PT]
full_text:
In a quiet village lived a gentle, simple-minded weaver named Mantharaka, known to all as Soft because of his mild and compliant nature. One day, while weaving a heavy carpet, the wooden frame of his ancestral loom cracked and splintered beyond repair.

Shouldering his axe, Soft walked into the forest to find a sturdy tree of seasoned timber to hew a new loom-beam. Wandering to the seashore, he found a majestic, ancient shisham tree, tall, straight, and branchless for thirty cubits.

As the weaver raised his iron axe to strike the trunk, a luminous tree spirit emerged from the bark and pleaded: 'Hold your blow, gentle artisan! This ancient tree is my sacred dwelling. If you spare my home, I will grant you any boon your heart desires!'

Soft lowered his axe, bowed politely, and said: 'Revered spirit, I must consult my dear friend and my beloved wife before I choose my wish. Remain here, and I will return shortly.'

Soft hurried to the village and visited his friend, the town barber. Explaining the spirit's offer, Soft asked: 'What should I ask for, brother?'

The barber's eyes gleamed with ambition: 'Ask to be made King of this realm! You can rule from a golden palace, and make me your grand vizier!'

Soft replied: 'Kingship is a burden of endless wars, conspiracies, and sleepless nights. Let me consult my wife; women have great wisdom in domestic affairs.'

The barber warned: 'Never consult a woman on great matters! Women think only of petty vanities!'

Yet Soft returned home and asked his wife: 'Dearest, the tree spirit has granted me a wish. The barber advises me to ask for a kingdom. What is your counsel?'

The wife scoffed: 'A kingdom? Kings are assassinated by their brothers or overthrown by rebellions! Ask for something practical for your trade! You are a weaver with only two hands and one head; ask for another head and two more hands! With four hands and two heads, you can operate two looms simultaneously, weave twice as many carpets, earn double profits, and become the richest merchant in the province without the perils of a crown!'

Pleased by her advice, Soft ran back to the forest and called out: 'O Tree Spirit! Grant me two heads and four hands, so that I may weave with double speed!'

'Your wish is granted!' spoke the spirit.

Instantly, a second head sprouted from Soft's neck, and two additional muscular arms grew from his shoulders!

Rejoicing, Soft marched proudly back into the village to display his marvelous new body to his neighbors.

As he entered the village square, the terrified villagers mistook the four-armed, two-headed apparition for a demonic Rakshasa invading their homes. Crying: 'A monster! A demon has entered the town!' they rushed upon him with iron bars, heavy stones, and clubs, beating poor Soft to death on the spot.

Thus Vishnu Sharma taught:
"He who takes counsel of a fool to shape his fortune's choice,
Ignoring reason, prudence, and the wise preceptor's voice,
Shall find the granted wish transform to ruin in a breath,
And bring the double-headed fool to an untimely death."
moral: Do not consult foolish or greedy advisers when a great opportunity is placed in your hands. [PT]
